prompt: An analyst receives a case of premium wine from a corporate client shortly after publishing a favorable research report. Under the CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct, the analyst should most appropriately:

options.A: Accept the gift, as it was a token of appreciation for legitimate research work.
options.B: Accept the gift only after disclosing it to the employer, provided it does not compromise future independence and objectivity.
options.C: Decline the gift regardless of disclosure, since all gifts from clients are prohibited under the Standards.

explanation: Standard I(B) – Independence and Objectivity permits receipt of gifts from clients, provided the analyst discloses the benefit to their employer and the gift does not compromise — or appear to compromise — the analyst's independence. A blanket prohibition (C) is too restrictive; the Standards focus on disclosure and whether objectivity is impaired. Silent acceptance (A) violates the disclosure requirement.
